class.name: VehiclePhysicsNode
class.brief_description: A vehicle's presence in the scene tree.
class.description: The vehicle itself is an object of [VehicleServer], addressed by a RID; this node owns that handle, builds the vehicle from a copy of its controller - a [VehicleController] with its components, the vehicle's stored configuration - and frees it. It is the anchor everything in the tree hangs off - a scripted component a modder adds, a cabin, a sound bank - so that "which vehicle am I part of" is answered by where a node sits, not by a path it carries. It knows nothing about where the controller came from: it is given one, or a subclass builds one ([code]_build_controller()[/code]).

method.name: _build_controller
method.description: The controller a node that was given none builds its vehicle from, as it enters the tree - once, before anything can see the vehicle.

method.name: add_component
method.description: Adds [param component] to this vehicle - what a proxy node in the tree calls when it joins, so a modder's component reaches the vehicle it sits under.

method.name: get_vehicle_rid
method.description: This vehicle's handle, for anything that talks to the servers.

members.member: The vehicle's configuration, a VehicleController its simulation is built from a copy of; a new one rebuilds the vehicle. The running copy is the vehicle's ([method VehicleServer.vehicle_get_controller]).
The velocity the vehicle starts with ([method VehicleServer.vehicle_set_initial_velocity]), set every time it is built.
The vehicle's id ([code]VehicleServer.vehicle_set_id()[/code]), set every time it is built. Not derived from whatever file the description came from - a scenery names its vehicles, a .fiz does not.

signal.name: vehicle_changed
signal.description: The vehicle was built, or rebuilt on another controller.
